name: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
evidence_rating: very thin: forecasts plus implementation milestones and vendor surveys; no independent evidence on incidents, resilience or costs
summary: DORA aims to make banks, insurers and other financial firms withstand IT failures and cyber attacks, and to oversee their key tech suppliers. Since it applied in January 2025, regulators have mapped firms' IT supply chains and put 19 critical providers - including the big cloud companies - under direct oversight. The forecast savings and reduction in incident costs have not been measured; the only cost evidence comes from vendor surveys suggesting many firms spent over EUR 1 million on compliance.

indicators.objective: The DORA proposal's financial statement contains no objectives or indicators section in the extracted text; the memorandum only provides for a Commission review three years after entry into force

indicators.indicator: Mitigate operational-incident costs for the EU financial sector (estimated EUR 2-27bn a year)
indicators.evidence: Not measured. DORA applies since 17 Jan 2025; no published statistics yet on incident numbers or costs under the new reporting regime.

indicators.indicator: Savings from removing overlapping incident reporting (EUR 40-100m a year for some of the largest banks)
indicators.evidence: Not measured. Industry surveys report high compliance costs: 38% of EU CISOs surveyed by Rubrik reported over EUR 1m spent on DORA/PRA compliance over two years; 37% of firms in a Veeam-commissioned survey face higher costs passed on by ICT vendors. No evidence on reporting savings.

indicators.indicator: Threat-led penetration testing cost 0.1-0.3% of ICT budget of firms concerned
Registers of information collected; critical ICT third-party providers designated and overseen
indicators.evidence: Dry run (2024): 1,039 entities took part, only 6.5% of 947 analysed registers passed all data-quality checks. First 19 critical providers designated on 18 Nov 2025 (incl. AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, Deutsche Telekom, Bloomberg, LSEG Data).
Survey evidence only: a vendor-commissioned survey six months in found 96% of EMEA respondents felt their data resilience fell short; ENISA 2024: 84% of entities expect to need more staff for DORA.

literature.citation: European Commission (2020), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (executive summary SWD(2020) 199), SWD(2020) 198
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (executive summary SWD(2020) 199)
literature.outcomes: incident costs; reporting burden; testing costs
literature.headline: Operational incident costs for EU financial sector estimated at EUR 2-27bn a year (industry assessments), which DORA would mitigate; removing overlapping reporting could save some of the largest banks EUR 40-100m a year; threat-led penetration testing 0.1-0.3% of ICT budget; one-off IT costs hard to quantify
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected DORA to curb ICT incidents that may cost EU finance EUR 2-27 billion a year and to save the biggest banks up to EUR 100 million a year in duplicate reporting.

literature.citation: EBA, EIOPA & ESMA (Joint Committee) (2024), DORA dry run exercise on reporting of registers of information - summary report, ESA 2024 35, 17 Dec 2024
literature.title: DORA dry run exercise on reporting of registers of information - summary report
literature.headline: 1,039 financial entities participated; of 947 registers analysed only 6.5% passed all 116 data-quality checks; missing mandatory information made up 86% of errors
literature.summary_plain: In a 2024 test run, only 6.5% of financial firms' registers of their IT suppliers passed all quality checks, showing how little firms knew about their dependencies.

literature.citation: EBA, EIOPA & ESMA (2025), List of designated critical ICT third-party service providers under DORA, ESAs publication, 18 Nov 2025
literature.title: List of designated critical ICT third-party service providers under DORA
literature.headline: 19 providers designated as critical (Accenture, AWS, Bloomberg, Capgemini, Colt, Deutsche Telekom, Equinix, FIS, Google Cloud, IBM, InterXion, Kyndryl, LSEG Data, Microsoft, NTT DATA, Oracle, Orange, SAP, TCS) based on registers of information
literature.summary_plain: In November 2025 EU regulators put 19 tech suppliers to banks and insurers - including the big cloud providers - under direct oversight.

literature.citation: ENISA (2024), NIS Investments 2024 (section on readiness for DORA and other legislation), ENISA report, Nov 2024
literature.title: NIS Investments 2024 (section on readiness for DORA and other legislation)
literature.headline: 84% of surveyed organisations will need additional cybersecurity staff to comply with DORA (89% for NIS2, 85% for CRA)
literature.summary_plain: Most organisations surveyed by ENISA said DORA will require them to hire more security staff.
literature.quality: self-reported; not limited to financial entities

literature.citation: Rubrik Zero Labs (reported by Infosecurity Magazine) (2025), DORA Compliance Costs Soar Past EUR 1m for Many UK and EU Businesses, Infosecurity Magazine, 16 Jan 2025
literature.authors: Rubrik Zero Labs (reported by Infosecurity Magazine)
literature.title: DORA Compliance Costs Soar Past EUR 1m for Many UK and EU Businesses
literature.headline: 38% of EU (47% of UK) CISOs said their organisation spent over EUR 1m on DORA/PRA compliance in 24 months; 30% of EU respondents EUR 501k-1m
literature.summary_plain: A vendor survey found more than a third of EU financial security chiefs had spent over EUR 1 million preparing for DORA.
literature.quality: vendor survey; mixes DORA with UK rules
literature.interested_party: Rubrik sells data-resilience software marketed for DORA compliance

literature.citation: Censuswide for Veeam Software (reported by Help Net Security) (2025), Six months into DORA, most financial firms are still not ready, Help Net Security, 25 July 2025
literature.authors: Censuswide for Veeam Software (reported by Help Net Security)
literature.title: Six months into DORA, most financial firms are still not ready
literature.method: survey of senior IT decision-makers in UK, FR, DE, NL
literature.headline: 96% say their data resilience is not where it needs to be; 37% face higher costs passed on by ICT vendors; 22% see digital regulation as a barrier to innovation or competition; about a quarter had not implemented incident reporting or resilience testing
literature.summary_plain: Six months after DORA applied, a vendor survey found most financial firms still felt unprepared, and over a third faced higher prices from IT suppliers.
literature.quality: vendor survey; sample size not stated
